name: Zed agent

surfaces.label: Zed editor: Agent Panel + Threads Sidebar. ONE Zed process hosts every Zed Agent thread and every external-agent thread; there is no per-thread process.

Zed Preview / Nightly / Dev: bundle names contain a space, so agents_probe.py (ps args split on spaces) sees the executable as just /Applications/Zed and the Preview/Nightly/Dev path_contains above can never match. This entry keys on the path prefix plus the rest of the path arriving as argv[1]. The Contents/MacOS/cli terminal command has no arg containing Contents/MacOS/zed, so it does not match. A detector that reads the full executable path can rely on the first entry alone.
External agent over ACP: one child process of Zed per connected agent (registry npx agents run under node, registry binary agents run directly). Speaks JSON-RPC on stdio.
Terminal Threads: an ordinary pty shell under Zed running any CLI/TUI. No Zed-specific process; the CLI matches its own registry row, with Zed as an ancestor.

working_signals.name: Agent thread in progress
working_signals.meaning: Zed takes it (NSProcessInfo beginActivityWithOptions UserInitiated) while an agent thread has a turn running (Zed Agent AND external ACP agents share this code) and drops it when the turn ends OR the thread blocks on a tool confirmation or question. One assertion per running, unblocked thread, all owned by the same pid, so it counts threads but cannot name them. Default on (agent.prevent_idle_sleep = true); if the user turns it off there is no assertion and this signal is silent. Read from source and docs, not observed: Zed is not installed here.

Zed Agent (native) threads only, UNVERIFIED: the native agent re-saves the thread into ~/Library/Application Support/Zed/threads/threads.db every time the thread entity changes, so the db (or its -wal file) mtime moves during a turn. One shared file for all threads and it says nothing about external agents. The probe cannot use it because there is no per_session path.

waiting_signals.meaning: While a thread waits for tool confirmation or an elicitation question, Zed releases the assertion (is_waiting_for_confirmation in acp_thread). From outside, waiting looks the same as idle at the OS level. Zed itself shows a popup window titled 'Waiting for tool confirmation' or 'Waiting for input' and bounces the Dock icon (agent.notify_when_agent_waiting, default primary_screen), but neither is readable by another process.
No hook, log line or file records the waiting state for a third party. In-app only: 'dev: open acp logs' shows ACP messages between Zed and an external agent.

hooks.config: Zed has no agent lifecycle hooks. The only hook is a task hook, create_worktree, in tasks.json (~/.config/zed/tasks.json or .zed/tasks.json), which fires after Zed creates a linked git worktree and says nothing about turns. External agents may have their own hooks (for example Claude Code settings.json hooks) but whether they run under the ACP wrapper was not checked.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry exporter found in Zed's docs or root Cargo.toml. Zed sends its own telemetry to Zed servers (Sentry, Snowflake), controlled by telemetry.diagnostics and telemetry.metrics in settings.json; audit with 'zed: open telemetry log'. An external agent may export OTel by itself if its env is set through agent_servers.<id>.env in Zed settings (not tested).

sources.claim: Zed asks the OS not to idle-sleep only while a thread is generating, not while it waits for confirmation; setting agent.prevent_idle_sleep turns it off

the assertion is taken per AcpThread with reason "Agent thread in progress" when running_turn is set, prevent_idle_sleep is true and the thread is not waiting for confirmation; AcpThread is the shared thread type for the Zed Agent and external ACP agents
sources.evidence: zed-industries/zed crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs: fn update_idle_sleep_prevention (cx.prevent_idle_sleep("Agent thread in progress")), fn is_waiting_for_confirmation, ThreadStatus::Generating when running_turn.is_some()

sources.claim: on macOS prevent_idle_sleep is NSProcessInfo beginActivityWithOptions with NSActivityOptions::UserInitiated, which includes idle system sleep disabled; the separate prevent_app_nap uses UserInitiatedAllowingIdleSystemSleep and does not
sources.evidence: zed-industries/zed crates/gpui_macos/src/platform.rs fn prevent_idle_sleep; crates/gpui_macos/src/dispatcher.rs fn prevent_app_nap and MacActivity::begin. That UserInitiated shows as PreventUserIdleSystemSleep in pmset is Apple's documented flag composition, not observed here. Local check 2026-09-29: pmset -g assertions on this Mac lists Chrome's IOPMAssertion as 'NoIdleSleepAssertion named: "Playing audio"' but caffeinate and Insomnia as 'PreventUserIdleSystemSleep named: ...', so the type label pmset prints for an NSProcessInfo activity is NOT confirmed. Match on owner pid plus the name string 'Agent thread in progress', not on the type label alone.

Offline matches() calls with synthetic ps lines: /Applications/Zed.app/Contents/MacOS/zed -> ide; '/Applications/Zed Preview.app/Contents/MacOS/zed' -> no match before the added Preview/Nightly/Dev surface, match after; Contents/MacOS/cli -> no match; node/opencode/claude-sdk lines containing Zed/external_agents/registry/ -> daemon; unrelated node and ~/Library/Application Support/Claude processes -> no match. classify() in tools/agents_probe.py has no branch for signal power_assertion, and transcript_write needs per_session, so the probe reports every Zed process idle.

notes: Zed is one process, so 'working' is per Zed window set, not per session. Best signal: a PreventUserIdleSystemSleep-class assertion owned by the Zed pid named 'Agent thread in progress' (count = running threads, dropped while a thread waits for you). The pmset type label is unconfirmed, key on pid and name. LIMIT OF THE PROBE: tools/agents_probe.py does not implement power_assertion, so under the probe every Zed and Zed-child row reads idle; the row is correct data for a detector that reads assertions (IOPMCopyAssertionsByProcess). CAVEAT for the other rows: a Claude agent under Zed runs as node -> claude-agent-acp -> the Claude Agent SDK's bundled native `claude` binary (package/claude in @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64); likewise codex under Zed runs a native codex. A detector that takes the executable name from the real path (proc_pidpath) sees name `claude` and the claude-code row would report a TUI session. agents_probe.py does NOT: the install path contains 'Application Support', ps args are split on spaces, so its exe is '/Users/<u>/Library/Application' and neither claude-code surface matches (checked offline); the Zed ACP surface matches it instead, and the probe's parent-dedup then drops it because its parent node also matches. Suppress by checking for a Zed ancestor (Zed.app/Contents/MacOS/zed) or a process whose path is under Application Support/Zed/external_agents. The ACP surface's path_contains '/Library/Application' is a deliberate hack: agents_probe.py splits args on spaces, so 'Application Support' is cut and only the args_contain check on 'Zed/external_agents/registry/' is discriminating; do not reuse that path_contains alone. The same space-splitting is why the second ide surface exists (Zed Preview/Nightly/Dev). Gaps: custom agents (agent_servers type custom) and legacy extension agents do not live under external_agents/registry/, so the ACP surface will not see them; they still count in the Zed process's assertions. Dev builds run from target/ bundles are not covered by the path patterns. The ide surface reports Zed whenever it is open, agents or not. Session mapping: no session id in argv; ACP session ids travel over stdio, so a process cannot be mapped to a thread from outside.
